sentences.text: Bacteroides clarus was proposed as a novel species for strain YIT 12056, one of three Gram-stain-negative, obligately anaerobic, non-spore-forming, rod-shaped bacteria isolated from human faeces.
The description reports menaquinones MK-10 and MK-11 as the major respiratory quinones of these isolates, properties typical for members of the genus Bacteroides.
A study of children reported that the abundance of Bacteroides clarus was higher in non-stunted children than in stunted children.
A strain-level screening reported that culture supernatant from a Bacteroides clarus strain strongly inhibited the growth of V. cholerae.
